claims.claim: Median income derived purely from farming for U.S. households was negative $1,830 as of 2024.
claims.method: Not recorded; source and population definition require review.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown until source, sampling frame, and inflation basis are checked.

claims.claim: Chapter 12 farm bankruptcies rose 55% in the prior year.
claims.date_scope: Prior year relative to article publication
claims.method: Not recorded; bankruptcy series and comparison period require review.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown until denominator and reporting period are checked.
Unknown date, nominal/real basis, and debt-series definition.

claims.claim: A cohort managing approximately 25 million acres reports profit margins 70% to 120% higher than conventional neighbors.
claims.method: Not recorded; cohort, comparator, and margin definition require review.
claims.uncertainty: High until population, selection effects, and calculation are established.

claims.claim: Regenerative farms survive droughts with 31% higher yields and cut input costs by half.
claims.units: percent yield difference; percent cost reduction
claims.method: Not recorded; crop, geography, baseline, and study design require review.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown; causal attribution is not established.

claims.claim: The transition period may last 3 to 5 years and profits may dip by 60% before increasing.
claims.uncertainty: Material variation is expected by crop, farm, market, and practice.

claims.claim: Conventional tilled fields absorb about 0.5 inches of rain per hour while regenerative no-till fields can absorb up to 8 inches.
claims.method: Requires field measurement protocol and soil/site controls.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown; rates are site- and event-dependent.

claims.claim: Organic regenerative corn yields were 31% higher than conventional corn during drought years.
claims.method: Requires crop, geography, treatment, and comparison definition.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown until matched comparison and drought definition are checked.

claims.claim: Gabe Brown is described as having recovered from $1.5 million in debt, increased soil organic matter from 1.9% to 6.1%, and exceeded county yield averages by 25%.
claims.units: USD; percent soil organic matter; percent yield difference
claims.method: Requires primary farm records or independently attributable case-study source.
claims.uncertainty: Unknown; anecdotal case cannot establish general effect.

claims.claim: A Nutrient Density Index (NDI) is proposed as a hybrid, tiered scoring system for legal and procurement use.
claims.method: Design proposal; not an adopted standard.
claims.uncertainty: Requires stakeholder, legal, scientific, and procurement review.

claims.claim: The proposed NDI-Core tier assigns a 40% weight to macronutrients and ten essential minerals per 100 kcal, with deductions for nutrients of concern.
claims.uncertainty: Weights, analytes, thresholds, and deductions are not validated.

claims.claim: The proposed NDI-Phyto tier assigns a 50% weight to bioactive compounds such as carotenoids and phenolics.
claims.method: Proposed weighted matrix; laboratory reference calibration contemplated.
claims.uncertainty: Health relevance, analyte panel, and weight are unvalidated.

claims.claim: The proposed NDI-Contaminant tier assigns a negative 10% weight and treats readings above legal limits as failure conditions.
claims.method: Proposed safety rule requiring legal-limit mapping.
claims.uncertainty: Applicable limits, sampling, and enforcement process are unspecified.

claims.claim: Spectral fingerprints could be correlated with laboratory reference methods to estimate chemical composition.
claims.method: Requires commodity-specific calibration and reference sampling.
claims.uncertainty: Prediction error, drift, matrix effects, and transferability are unknown.

claims.claim: A defensible chemometric model should publish calibration populations, uncertainty ranges, drift checks, and commodity-specific limits.
claims.uncertainty: Implementation thresholds and acceptance criteria require expert review.

claims.claim: A high R² alone is insufficient to establish procurement-grade measurement evidence.
claims.method: Requires validation against accepted measurement-science and procurement criteria.
claims.uncertainty: Exact criteria depend on intended use and risk tolerance.

claims.claim: External validation, reproducibility, and chain of custody are proposed requirements for procurement evidence.
claims.uncertainty: Protocols and pass/fail thresholds are not yet specified.

claims.claim: Organic and regenerative labels do not automatically establish continuous auditability or correlation with human-health outcomes.
claims.uncertainty: The claim varies by certification, audit regime, commodity, and outcome.
